facts.fact: A University of Abomey-Calavi law lecturer, presenting to MPs on 12 January 2024, lists artificial intelligence among the missed appointments of the Code du numerique, which does not address it.

BEN.note: Nothing stated on AI used by a government body.
Nothing stated on AI in a sector's public system.
Nothing stated on AI built or hosted.
Only the Code's rules on trust service providers and electronic evidence are mentioned; no service stated.

systems.system: Agence des Systemes d'Information et du Numerique (ASIN)

BEN.note: ASIN, created by decree 2022-324 of 1 June 2022 merging ADN, ASSI, ANSSI and ABSUCEP, is named but its cybersecurity role is not described.

facts.fact: The lecturer's deck says the Code du numerique (arts 392, 411, 467) provides for the Autorite de protection des donnees personnelles (APDP), whose powers the Council of Ministers' authorisation role weakens and for which no mechanism covers a prolonged vacancy of a member or the president.
The lecturer says the Code du numerique (Loi 2017-20 of 20 April 2018, amended 2020, 647 articles) regulates personal data protection in Book 5 and has been applied for five years.
The deck says the Code names the Autorite de protection des donnees personnelles (APDP) as supervisory authority.

The lecturer says the Code du numerique (Loi 2017-20 of 20 April 2018, amended 2020) governs electronic commerce, electronic writings and tools and trust service providers, with article 268 setting conditions for electronic evidence.

BEN.note: Open data is only named as a gap in the Code; no published data stated.
Article 550 criticised as vague; no one is reported charged and no cut stated.

facts.fact: Dr Julien Hounkpe, lecturer at the University of Abomey-Calavi and researcher at its CREDIJ, presented a critique of the Code du numerique to MPs at a National Assembly workshop in Porto-Novo on 12 January 2024 on revising the Code.
The deck says the Code du numerique does not internalise the ECOWAS Additional Act of 16 February 2010 on personal data protection, treating it as part of the community legal order that binds Benin.
facts.system: ECOWAS Additional Act on personal data protection
